home.role: Analyst. Chess player. Athlete. Average salesman.
home.intro: I do BI for retail at Albert. Outside work I coach chess, run marathons and organise things nobody asked me to.
home.aboutP1: I make a living with data in retail, currently as a BI Analyst at Albert. I studied at the Prague University of Economics and Business, where my master's thesis looked at how Czech companies adopt AI in practice.
home.aboutP2: Outside work I'm a FIDE Master, I run marathons and I sit on the board of Young Ahold Delhaize, the employee network at Albert. At university I spent over four years organising sports events with the 4FIS association and working as a student ambassador. I enjoy bringing people together, whether it's a tournament or a workshop. I like to travel and see how things are done elsewhere.
home.tagline: FIDE Master, marathon runner, and someone who cannot do hobbies casually.
home.heroNote: This site mostly fills in what my friends already know about me. If you're not one of them yet, this is a good start. As for why I do so much of it, you won't find the answer here. I don't know either.
home.heroProfession: By day I build data models and reports at Albert that people use to make decisions in four countries. In the evenings I coach chess, run, or organise something for others.
home.nowBi: BI Analyst at Albert. Comparing loyalty metrics across retail brands and building reports for management in four countries. Databricks, PySpark, Power BI.
home.nowAi: Thesis on how eight Czech companies adopt AI. Now mostly testing what LLMs actually help with in analytical work.
home.nowSide: This site, App Compare and a few other things I enjoy building.
home.nowChess: FIDE Master. Coach and occasional player.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: I run this website as a private individual, not a company. Here's a plain summary of how I handle information you send me through it.
privacy.formsText: The site has three forms: booking, contact, and an inspiration tip. Submitted details (name, email, and message where relevant) are sent as a notification to my Discord and stored in a database I use to read and work with them.
privacy.storageText: Form data is stored with Sanity (CMS) and sent via Discord (notifications) and Resend (booking confirmation emails). I don't sell or share this data with any of these providers for advertising purposes.
privacy.protectionText: Forms are protected by Cloudflare Turnstile against automated spam. The site runs over a secure HTTPS connection.
privacy.rightsText: If you'd like me to delete information you submitted through any of the forms, email me at petr@hollan.eu and I'll take care of it.
privacy.disclaimer: I'm not a lawyer and this page isn't legal advice, it's a plain-language summary of how the site works.

appCompare.title: App comparison
appCompare.lead: Paste links from the App Store or Google Play, choose a country and track ratings, review counts and trends over time. No login, API keys or manual Excel work required.
appCompare.trendDesc: Average star rating of all reviews per month. Shows whether user satisfaction is improving or declining over time.
appCompare.barsDesc: Bar chart showing how many reviews came in each month and what star ratings the app received. Color-coded 1–5 stars.
appCompare.reviewsLimit: App Store RSS allows downloading a maximum of 500 most recent reviews. Apple does not provide a public API for older reviews.
appCompare.step1Desc: App Store or Google Play. Ratings and reviews can differ significantly between markets.
appCompare.step2Desc: Compare up to five apps at once. Just copy their URLs — app IDs are detected automatically.
appCompare.step3Desc: Get the basic comparison straight away. Then load individual reviews, see how ratings develop month by month and export data as CSV for further analysis.
appCompare.forWhoTitle: What can you use it for
appCompare.forWho: For example, to find out how your app compares with competitors, whether user ratings are improving or getting worse over time, how results differ across markets, or what users keep mentioning in their reviews.
appCompare.origin: I originally built it for my own use when comparing mobile apps. Then I figured it was more useful here than sitting on my laptop.
appCompare.ctaDesc: Custom scraping, data pipeline or AI-powered review analysis — happy to take a look.
